instructions: Blackwall is an autonomous Agentic Security Firewall designed to intercept execution flows at machine speed before rogue AI agents can perform unauthorized OS/network actions. The primary entry point is the Blackwall MCP Gateway — a standalone local daemon (Architectural Specification governed by .kiro/specs/blackwall-mcp-gateway/ - target paths src/blackwall/gateway/ + src/blackwall/cli.py) that intercepts MCP tool calls on localhost:9229 and evaluates them via the SyncResolver pipeline. External threat intelligence is powered by an in-process AlienVault OTX integration (10,000 req/hr, ~166 RPM token bucket, 3-state circuit breaker, SQLite threat_intel_cache with <1ms SLA, and harpoon OSINT companion bridge governed by .kiro/specs/blackwall-threat-intel-cli/), replacing the 4 RPM VirusTotal GTI bottleneck; no VirusTotal client ships in src/blackwall/threat_intel/ and BW_THREAT_INTEL_BACKEND is inert (BW_THREAT_INTEL_PRIMARY=harpoon|harpoon-otx selects the Harpoon companion bridge). Verify architecture invariants across Blackwall Core (single-host daemon + MCP Gateway) and Blackwall Enterprise Mesh (multi-host security mesh under src/blackwall/enterprise/). The gateway MUST NOT contain agent-specific coupling (no Hermes, no Antigravity-specific, no Warp-specific logic). Ensure strict Pydantic v2 validation, GCP Vertex AI Mode compliance for Tier-2 reasoning, forensics, and evaluation judges (paid tier only, no free tier, no AI Studio keys) alongside the approved Tier-1 Jev classifier via paid Vercel AI Gateway credits (AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY with disallowPromptTraining on every call and sanitization-before-egress, governed by .kiro/specs/tier-1-jev-addition/), TDD/BDD test coverage, cross-platform background service management (macOS launchd and Linux systemd on DGX OS / Ubuntu), and resource budget compliance across dual hardware profiles: 2019 Intel MacBook Pro (baseline) and NVIDIA DGX Spark (top-of-the-line GB10 ARM64, 0MB CUDA, host RSS <= 350MB). Windows OS support is strictly excluded.

rules.rule: Vendor Compliance (Vertex Tier-2/Forensics/Eval + Approved Tier-1 Jev): Google Gemini usage MUST be 100% GCP Vertex AI Mode (Paid Tier Only): google-genai clients instantiate with vertexai=True, require GCP_PROJECT / GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT via Application Default Credentials (ADC). Flag any PR reintroducing Google AI Studio API key configurations (GEMINI_API_KEY, LLM_API_KEY, BACKUP_LLM_API_KEY), Vertex free-tier fallbacks (e.g. 15 RPM caps), or standard-tier rate limit logic. EXCEPTION — Tier-1 Jev backend (governed by .kiro/specs/tier-1-jev-addition/): use of AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY with paid Vercel AI Gateway Credits for typesafe-ai/jev is APPROVED. Do NOT flag AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY, bounded 429 backoff with fail-closed behavior in the Jev backend, or paid-credit operation as violations. Flag any Jev call missing disallowPromptTraining:true, any unsanitized payload egress to the Gateway, or free-tier reliance for production traffic. Note: External threat intelligence in Blackwall 3.0 runs via AlienVault OTX (10,000 req/hr token bucket, ~166 RPM) with SQLite caching (<1ms SLA). Legacy VirusTotal GTI is NOT implemented: no VT client ships in src/blackwall/threat_intel/ and BW_THREAT_INTEL_BACKEND is read by no code path; BW_THREAT_INTEL_PRIMARY=harpoon|harpoon-otx selects the Harpoon companion bridge instead.

Threat Intelligence Engine & Native CLI Invariants: Verify threat intelligence components (governed by .kiro/specs/blackwall-threat-intel-cli/) enforce: (1) In-process AlienVaultOTXProvider with 10,000 req/hr capacity (~166 RPM token bucket, 0.36s replenishment) authenticated via BW_OTX_API_KEY or ~/.blackwall/config.yaml, with 1,000 req/hr unauthenticated fallback and warning log; (2) 3-state circuit breaker requiring 3 consecutive successful probes in HALF-OPEN mode before restoring to CLOSED, immediately resetting to OPEN upon failure; (3) Typed exception propagation (OTXCircuitBreakerOpenError, OTXTokenBucketExhaustedError, OTXLookupError) on outages and rate exhaustion without masking failures as benign; (4) URL and credential redaction (_sanitize_indicator_for_log) preventing secrets/passwords from persisting in logs; (5) Persistent SQLite threat_intel_cache in WAL mode with < 1ms SLA (24h benign / 6h malicious TTL) and automatic purge on repository initialization; (6) Harpoon OSINT bridge and native blackwall check / threat-intel CLI commands.

Core Tier Architecture & Zero-eBPF Integrity: Verify Blackwall Core (src/blackwall/ outside enterprise/) remains a lightweight single-host daemon containing zero imports or dependencies on ZeroMQ, NATS, or eBPF C headers.

Enterprise Subsystem Modularization: Verify all enterprise capabilities (eBPF kernel probes, ZeroMQ threat mesh, Vault sidecars, sandboxes, forensic engine, advanced threat detection) are cleanly isolated under src/blackwall/enterprise/.

Enterprise Boundary Review Scope: For code under src/blackwall/enterprise/, review only for Core/Enterprise boundary violations and shared interface compatibility. Do not flag Enterprise-internal pillar implementations (eBPF drivers, ZeroMQ mesh, Vault sidecar, pipeline wrappers, forensics engine) as violations — these are intentional Enterprise-only features.

Advanced Threat Detection (Pillar 6) Isolation & Model Validation: Verify Pillar 6 components (including ActiveReactionEngine, InboundProtocolFilter, PromptInjectionScanner, AgentQuotaEnforcer) reside under src/blackwall/enterprise/advanced_threat_detection/ and Pydantic v2 data models enforce UUID v4 identifiers, UTC timezone awareness with zero offset (utcoffset == 0), score bounds [0.0, 1.0], non-negative usage limits, string enums, and mandatory evidence-derived evaluation containment.

Async Interception Pipeline Resolver Order: Verify SyncResolver execution flow strictly maintains: Rate Check -> ContextHygiene Sanitization -> Threat Signature Graph (TSG) Check -> Codebase Memory MCP AST Query -> Threat Intelligence Validation (AlienVault OTX / Multi-Provider Orchestrator) -> Semantic Triage via pluggable jev|gemini backend (Tier-1 Jev P(threat) with 0.35/0.75 ambiguity band escalating to Gemini Tier-2, governed by .kiro/specs/tier-1-jev-addition/) -> Score Aggregation -> Threshold Verdict. Structural policy checks MUST NOT early-return or short-circuit stages prior to Score Aggregation.

Production Model Standards & Structured Outputs: Rapid triage defaults to the Tier-1 Jev classifier (typesafe-ai/jev) fronting SemanticTriageProvider, with gemini-3.5-flash-lite retained as fallback/legacy backend; deep reasoning remains gemini-3.8-flash. PHASED ROLLOUT EXCEPTION (.kiro/specs/tier-1-jev-addition/): BW_SEMANTIC_BACKEND intentionally defaults to gemini from TASK-A02 and a configured jev degrades to gemini with a warning until the Jev backend ships in TASK-B01; the default flips to jev only in TASK-D04 after the Track-D A/B gate passes. Do NOT flag a pre-D04 PR for keeping gemini as the default or for the fail-closed jev-to-gemini degradation, but DO flag any PR that flips the default to jev before TASK-D04 or that makes an unimplemented backend raise / silently disable triage. Flag any PR using legacy/deprecated models (gemini-3.1-*, gemini-2.*, gemini-1.5-*, or Gemini Pro models). Gemini triage and signature generation must enforce native structured outputs (response_schema, response_mime_type="application/json") and prohibit manual regex JSON extraction and defensive negative prompt scaffolding. The Jev backend is EXEMPT from response_schema (evaluation models return typed answers, not text) — instead verify a single boolean is_threat question, fixed 0.35/0.75 thresholds, and disallowPromptTraining:true on every call.
SQL Parameterization Hygiene: Flag any SQL query that interpolates variables directly into an f-string without parameterized bindings. All dynamic values must be passed as bound parameters.

Synthetic Honey-Token & Secret Masking Compliance: Environment variable readers in src/blackwall/enterprise/identity/ must replace sensitive credentials (AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, KUBECONFIG) with synthetic honey-tokens (BW_SYNTHETIC_*) and route JIT swaps via hashicorp-vault-mcp.

Forensic Engine Dual-Mode & AST Resolution Integrity: Verify ForensicTriageEngine supports primary Ollama open-weight LLM triage with automatic failover to LightweightForensicParser when GPU/Ollama is offline. Ensure LightweightForensicParser AST inspection resolves fully qualified callee names (e.g. os.system, subprocess.Popen) rather than bare attribute names.

Test-Driven Development (TDD) & BDD Coverage: Flag any PR modifying src/ without corresponding unit or integration tests under tests/, property-based tests under tests/property/, and BDD feature scenarios in tests/features/.

Secret Scanner Hygiene in Test Artifacts: Ensure test files contain no live cloud credential patterns or high-entropy secret prefixes (e.g. AWS_KEY_<digits>). Intentional adversarial vectors in redaction test suites (tests/test_report_generator.py, tests/eval/test_data/) that assert placeholder substitution are expected fixtures and MUST NOT be flagged as leaked secrets.
Process Group Cleanup & Audit Hook Scoping: Verify sys.addaudithook registrations in tests are deferred to function scope and background test processes clean up process groups via os.killpg.

Attacker Identification & Reporting Integrity: Verify Attacker Identification & Reporting components (AttackerIdentityExtractor, AttackerProfile, IncidentReportGenerator) enforce Pydantic v2 validation (SHA-256 fingerprint, UTC timestamps, [0.0, 1.0] risk scores), process sanitized context, and fail-closed cleanly.

MCP Gateway Architecture Invariants: Verify gateway components under src/blackwall/gateway/ (Architectural Specification per .kiro/specs/blackwall-mcp-gateway/ - apply when implemented) enforce: (1) HTTP transport binds to 127.0.0.1 by default with Origin/Host header validation, (2) JSON-RPC request id tracking for concurrent call isolation, (3) BLOCK verdicts synthesize error code -32603 with bounded generic messages (no internal threat reasoning leaked), (4) ALLOW verdicts forward original payloads unchanged to downstream tool servers, (5) daemon mode writes PID to ~/.blackwall/blackwall.pid with graceful SIGTERM shutdown, (6) client _meta cannot spoof environment_role or security properties, and (7) policy configuration loading fails closed without un-gated fallback.

Gateway Agent Agnosticism: The MCP Gateway (specification targets src/blackwall/gateway/ and src/blackwall/cli.py per .kiro/specs/blackwall-mcp-gateway/) MUST NOT contain hardcoded references, special-case logic, or configuration for any specific agent runtime (Hermes Agent, Antigravity, Warp Terminal, Claude Desktop, Cursor, etc.). All agent interaction must be purely via standard MCP protocol. Flag any PR introducing agent-specific coupling in the gateway layer.

Gateway Resource Budgets (Dual Hardware Profiles): Blackwall Core gateway components (when implemented per .kiro/specs/blackwall-mcp-gateway/) must operate within: (1) 2019 Intel MacBook Pro Baseline: <=60MB idle RAM, <=150MB active RAM, ~0% idle CPU, <5% active CPU per call, <2s startup, <=50MB disk; (2) NVIDIA DGX Spark Top-of-the-Line (Grace Blackwell GB10 ARM64, 128GB unified memory): <=100MB idle RAM, <=350MB active RAM, 0MB CUDA context / VRAM allocation, host RSS bounded to <=350MB (<0.28% of unified pool) preserving >127.6GB (>99.7%) unified memory for local AI models, ~0% idle CPU, <2% active CPU across 20 cores, <1s startup. Flag PRs introducing polling loops, background threads, eager module loading, or GPU context allocations that violate these budgets.

PR Description Grouping: Group changes by Blackwall component: (1) MCP Gateway (specification: src/blackwall/gateway/, src/blackwall/cli.py), (2) Core Engine (SyncResolver, policy, threat graph, attribution), (3) Enterprise Mesh (src/blackwall/enterprise/). Highlight changes affecting security resolvers, protocol transports, eBPF probes, or MCP adapters.

Dual-Tiered GCP Evaluation Architecture & Zero-SaaS Invariants: Threat evaluation pipelines must use Tier 1 (ADK Adversarial Harness in 100% GCP Vertex AI mode) or Tier 2 (Cybench on Cloud Run with gVisor microVMs) with Google Cloud Vertex AI Gen AI Evaluation Service (EvalTask) and Google Cloud Trace. Third-party SaaS evaluation tokens (WANDB_API_KEY) and Weave dependencies are deprecated and prohibited. This zero-SaaS rule governs the evaluation harness and judges (Vertex/ADC only). It does NOT prohibit the approved production Tier-1 Jev backend via paid Vercel AI Gateway credits (governed by .kiro/specs/tier-1-jev-addition/), nor candidate-side Gateway credentials in A/B eval runs.

Performance & Async Safety: Focus code suggestions strictly on performance bottlenecks, thread safety, async coroutine safety, and security vulnerabilities. Ensure suggestions conform to Python 3.14 async patterns and avoid deprecated decorators like @unittest_run_loop.

Rust Acceleration & FFI Invariants: Verify native Rust optimizations in crates/blackwall_core_rs/ adhere to the non-greedy rewrite philosophy (90/10 to 95/5 rule). Ensure dual-mode context sanitization parity (Middleware full-match + SHA-256 vs Resolver prefix preservation), candidate isolation in batch cosine similarity, zero-panic PyResult error handling, and pure-Python fallbacks in all wrapping Python modules.

Cross-Platform Background Service Supervision & Packaging Invariants: Verify service management logic (blackwall service install|uninstall|start|stop|status|configure) enforces: (1) Supervised processes run blackwall serve --foreground (with Type=exec and PIDFile= in systemd) so supervisors directly track the active gateway without tracking exiting parents; (2) In foreground mode, --pidfile creates the designated PID file upon start and cleans up on exit; (3) Absolute path resolution (Path.resolve()) is enforced at install time so 0 raw ~ characters appear in service files; (4) systemd rate limits (StartLimitBurst=5, StartLimitIntervalSec=60s) belong strictly under [Unit], NOT [Service]; (5) Linux system units (--system) use FHS paths (/etc/blackwall/, /run/blackwall/, /var/log/blackwall/, /var/lib/blackwall/) via RuntimeDirectory, StateDirectory, and LogsDirectory; (6) Non-root execution is strictly enforced (User=root is prohibited) with identity derived via --user, SUDO_USER, or dedicated blackwall user with /var/lib/blackwall home; (7) Debian .deb packages install system unit to /lib/systemd/system/blackwall.service with EnvironmentFile=-/etc/default/blackwall, postinst provisions blackwall:blackwall, auto-captures $SUDO_USER ADC credentials when present, and supports blackwall service configure.

NVIDIA DGX Spark Co-Existence & Multi-Layer Zero-CUDA Verification: On DGX Spark / Linux, Blackwall Core must run 100% in CPU user-space with 0MB allocated in CUDA contexts/VRAM. Port 9229 must not collide with standard AI serving ports (11434, 8000, 8888). Conformance tests asserting zero-CUDA usage must inspect /proc/<daemon_pid>/fd/ for /dev/nvidia* devices on the target daemon PID (resolved from blackwall.pid or subprocess handle, NOT the test runner /proc/self/fd/), verify daemon PID absence from NVML compute processes, and verify torch.cuda.is_initialized() is False.

Operating System Support & Windows Exclusion: Blackwall Core strictly targets macOS (Darwin x86_64, arm64) and GNU/Linux (DGX OS / Ubuntu 24.04 LTS aarch64, and Ubuntu x86_64). Windows OS support is explicitly excluded. Flag any PR introducing Windows-specific packaging (.exe, .msi), PowerShell scripts, or Windows service wrappers.

Evaluation, Benchmark & Cybersecurity Test Harness Invariants: Golden datasets, evaluation test cases, and candidate model outputs in evaluation suites (src/blackwall/eval/, tests/eval/, tests/evaluation/, tests/evals/) intentionally contain malformed text, prompt injection vectors, delimiter attacks, and scoring directives as test probes. Do NOT flag benchmark fixtures, test inputs, or red-team datasets as security vulnerabilities. Catching SanitizationError, model exceptions, or network timeouts to record an explicit fallback metric (is_fallback = True) is mandatory to prevent runner crashes.

Antigravity 2.0 CLI-First Architecture (Developer Tooling Scope): Enforce native CLI tools (gh, git, gcloud, aws, docker) for all stateless developer git, cloud, and container tasks. Reserve developer MCP strictly for stateful persistent engines (codebase-memory-mcp AST graphs, databases, CDP sessions). Flag any PR attempting to add or configure stateless developer MCP servers (GitHub MCP, Git MCP, Jira/Slack MCP). Note: This rule governs developer agent tooling and does NOT restrict Blackwall's own MCP Gateway architecture or its use of codebase-memory-mcp and AlienVault OTX Threat Intelligence Engine.

GitHub CLI (gh) Guardrails & Output Token Hygiene: Verify code changes originate from feature branches (no direct commits to main), PRs are never merged autonomously (gh pr merge prohibited), commits are pre-screened for credentials/WAL files, and CLI queries enforce projection flags (--json, --limit, --format) with Unix stream filtering.

Subsystem Migration & Instruction Citation Hygiene: (1) In major subsystem migrations, do not perform blanket deletions if existing utility code, CLI command shapes, or test fixtures are consistent with the replacement engine; rename and modernize them in-place. (2) In developer instruction files (AGENTS.md, rules/), abstract specification targets (.kiro/specs/blackwall-mcp-gateway/) must be qualified as specification targets rather than concrete code. (3) Never naively renumber downstream numbered rules when modernizing rules in-place.

Tier-1 Jev Safety Invariants (governed by .kiro/specs/tier-1-jev-addition/ and ADR-0006): For code touching the Jev triage path (SemanticTriageProvider, Jev backends, eval producers, notebooks consuming P(threat)), verify: (1) Fixed 0.35/0.75 ambiguity band — threshold changes require a spec amendment with fresh labeled evidence; flag adjustable acceptance gates. (2) Aggregation supremacy — Jev outputs are weighted signals only; terminal ALLOW/BLOCK/QUARANTINE are decided exclusively at Score Aggregation + Threshold Verdict; flag any Jev-to-verdict short-circuit. (3) Every Gateway call sets disallowPromptTraining:true and builds state only from sanitized Tool/Arguments/Metadata; flag raw context, env-var, or credential egress, and ground-truth-bearing label text in eval inputs. (4) Async signature generation fires only for novel (non-TSG-matched) BLOCKs. (5) AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY persists only to 0600 env files, never inline in service definitions, logs, or unit files. (6) Caught model/API failures in eval rows record is_fallback:true.

Tier-1 Semantic Triage Seam Contract (Track A of .kiro/specs/tier-1-jev-addition/; codified in .agents/rules/architecture_and_security.md rule 106): Verify (1) SyncResolver._evaluate_semantic_intent remains an Optional[float] adapter returning SemanticTriageResult.threat_score — renaming it or returning the result object breaks tests/unit/test_sync_resolver_semantic_triage.py line 104, which patches that method, so treat that method name and signature as a compatibility surface. (2) Providers signal unavailability by returning None, never a synthetic 0.0, because _score_argument_novelty fail-closes through max() and a zero would erase a deterministic high-risk signal. (3) An unimplemented BW_SEMANTIC_BACKEND value logs a warning naming the owning task and degrades to the shipped gemini backend — flag any path that raises on an unknown backend or silently disables triage, and flag a default flip to jev before TASK-D04. (4) src/blackwall/policy/semantic.py intentionally hosts two unrelated subsystems, SemanticGatingEngine (agent-side async gating) and the Tier-1 triage seam; do not demand they be merged or share a verdict path.

Formatter, Baseline and Track-Scope Hygiene (codified in .agents/rules/testing_and_hygiene.md rule 73): (1) At target-version py314 both black 26.x and ruff format 0.16-plus rewrite a parenthesized except tuple into the PEP 758 unparenthesized form, which parses to the same AST on 3.14, so both spellings are valid and test-green. Do not flag either spelling as a syntax error or a regression, and do not demand a formatter sweep: roughly 284 files are formatter-dirty and pre-commit hooks are not installed in this checkout. (2) Failures in GCP/Vertex evaluation suites are frequently environmental rather than defects: .venv on Python 3.14.7 is the sole repository environment and is installed without the evaluation and eval optional extras. Require a baseline diff against pristine main before treating such a failure as introduced by the PR. (3) Where a spec track's own acceptance gates conflict with the repo-wide unit plus property plus BDD triad rule, the track scope governs; deferred coverage must be cited to the task that owns it instead of being pulled forward into the current track.
